description: Western North America soil-wetness replay over the full 397-cell nasa-power-0.5-degree lattice already established in agri.spatial_cell by the weather-fast plan (nasa-power-western-na-weather-fast-20220806-20260806, COMPLETE 397/397 in production). Carries the same three documented MERRA-2 soil-wetness depths as the four-cell southwest-Idaho probe (nasa-power-pnw-soil-wetness-20220805-20260805, verified COMPLETE 4/4): GWETTOP surface, GWETROOT root zone, GWETPROF profile, each a degree of saturation (fraction_of_saturation), not a volumetric water content. This is the keyless soil-moisture stream; the ERA5-Land volumetric path is blocked on a Copernicus dataset licence the account holder must accept in a browser. WIDENING 2026-08-08: NASA POWER serves GWETTOP/GWETROOT/GWETPROF on the same keyless daily point API as the fast meteorology parameters, across the same footprint -- the four-cell probe was a deliberate initial probe, not an upstream coverage limit, so this plan reuses the weather-fast lattice's exact 397 cell keys and coordinates verbatim (ST_Equals-checked, so it stays idempotent against the same agri.spatial_cell rows) and its exact window, rather than re-measuring a GWET-specific frontier. If NASA POWER's GWET latency differs from the fast-parameter latency measured for that plan, require_complete_nasa_result will fail closed per cell at run time rather than silently accepting a stale day. The probe plan is left in place, not superseded or deleted: HistoricalBackfillWindow requires an exact four-calendar-year span, so this plan's window necessarily re-covers the probe's four cells and days under a new source_release_id; uq_signal_observation_release_cell_signal_time includes source_release_id by design and downstream covariate reads already DISTINCT ON (signal_name, day) ORDER BY data_available_at DESC, so the overlap is safe by construction, matching the precedent recorded in the probe plan's own description.
